entity_title: Employer must register with ESD first
fact_text: A relocating professional cannot apply for a Malaysian Employment Pass themselves. The hiring company must first register with, and be approved by, the Immigration Department's Expatriate Services Division (ESD) before it can submit any expatriate pass application.
evidence_quote: All companies will need to register with the ESD as a first step.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the employee applies for their own Malaysian work visa. Actually the employer must first register and be approved with the ESD before any Employment Pass can be lodged. Action: confirm your employer already holds an active ESD account before agreeing a start date.

fact_text: Before a company can register with ESD to sponsor expatriates it must meet two requirements: incorporation with the Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM) and a minimum paid-up capital - RM250,000 for a 100% local-owned company, RM350,000 for a joint venture (minimum 30% foreign equity), or RM500,000 for a 100% foreign-owned company.
evidence_quote: There are two requirements needed before companies can proceed with the ESD registration.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any registered employer can sponsor a foreign hire. Actually the sponsoring company must clear a minimum paid-up-capital threshold (up to RM500,000 for a 100% foreign-owned entity) before ESD registration. Action: check that a newly incorporated or thinly capitalised employer can actually meet the capital gate.

entity_title: ESD company registration takes 14 working days
fact_text: Once complete documents are submitted, ESD company registration takes 14 working days. Because the employer must be registered before it can lodge an Employment Pass, this lead time sits before the individual's pass processing even begins.
evidence_quote: it takes fourteen (14) working days for the process to be completed.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work pass is issued within days of accepting an offer. Actually, if the employer is not yet ESD-registered, that registration alone takes 14 working days before any Employment Pass can be submitted. Action: ask whether the employer is already ESD-registered, or add 14+ working days up front.

entity_title: Director must sign Letter of Undertaking in person
fact_text: To activate its ESD account the company Director must attend in person to sign the Letter of Undertaking (LoU); no one may represent the Director. Until activation is complete the employer cannot submit expatriate applications.
evidence_quote: A company Director has to be present for the submission of the LoU.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed immigration onboarding can be fully delegated to HR or an agent. Actually a company Director must appear in person to sign the Letter of Undertaking before the ESD account is activated. Action: schedule the Director's LoU appointment early, as it blocks all pass submissions.

entity_title: EP categories I/II/III and revised salary thresholds
fact_text: The Employment Pass has three categories (I, II and III), each with its own minimum monthly salary threshold. A revised Employment Pass Salary Policy took effect on 1 June 2026, updating the minimum salary thresholds and adding a structured employment duration framework.
evidence_quote: updates to the minimum salary thresholds for Employment Pass (EP) Categories I, II, and III, as well as a structured employment duration framework.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed there is a single flat salary rule for a work visa. Actually eligibility depends on which of three EP categories the role falls into, and the thresholds were revised from 1 June 2026. Action: confirm the offered salary meets the current threshold for the intended EP category.
